## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e1d81c2a851a7d7a7565fc7d456feb658b81e390`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of the relay (the seats' internal write toolchain, not a published package): the closed op table gains exactly one row at its end, `workflow_dispatch` — `workflow` a closed enum over `WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_ALLOWLIST` (one file, `shard-timings-refresh.yml`, matched whole: a path, a dot-dot path, a glob and an off-list name each refused by name), `ref` a closed enum of exactly `main` (required, never defaulted), no `inputs` key (refused by name; the one allowlisted workflow declares none and the platform answers 422 to inputs on such a workflow), `alone: true` (a stroke carrying it carries exactly that one action; two in one stroke refused). Right: a closed addition, refused before dispatch on every malformed shape, and the ruling's option A as the maintainer gave it — 「22369 允许 actions: write」 (record 6078120063).
- The grant is minted for that stroke alone: `PERMISSIONS` gains `actions: write` and `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS = ['actions']`; `validate.mjs` computes `tokenPermissionsOf(payload)` and writes `permission_actions=write` for a run stroke, `permission_actions=` (empty) for every other, to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; `fleet-write.yml`'s mint step reads `permission-actions: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.permission_actions }}` and nothing else changes there (the four literal grants stay literal). The self-test pins both spellings against the workflow file on disk (a scoped grant spelled as a literal reds), and `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES` now carries a catch-all over every `actions/*` path but the one dispatch call plus the run / job / cache / artifact / enable-disable / secret-variable-runner families, with a 19-path positive control and the pin that the dispatch call is the ONLY `actions/*` path the whole table reaches. Right — least exposure by construction, one mint step, no `if:` fork.
- Confirmation by measure: the dispatch answers 204 with no body (`execute.mjs` reads it as `accepted (HTTP 204, no body)`; 422 and 403 are FAILED actions), so the seat side (`dispatch.mjs`) reads the started run back from the workflow's run list filtered to `event=workflow_dispatch&branch=main`, newest run created since the dispatch, re-read within a 60 s window; found is `landed` (id, url, actor; more than one candidate is SAID, never chosen silently); an unreadable list or none in the window is `unverified` → exit 6 UNCONFIRMED after ONE dispatch, never re-sent. Right: the existing vocabulary, and `ANNOTATED_OPS` rightly not used (its contract is a number read from the answer, and there is no answer).
- The merge behind the landed #22457 (`e1d81c2a`, parents `094be7b5` + `587bd969`, authored and committed by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, no history rewritten): the three-dot diff against `main` is the same six files (+434/−56); the landed `pr_update_branch` row, `confirmUpdateBranch`, `SHA_SHAPE` and the `update-branch` pin all survive on the head; both rows sit where the claims put them (`pr_update_branch` in the PR cluster, `workflow_dispatch` last, `OP_NAMES` read on the head); the battery floors are pinned at the counts the self-tests print (validate 10, execute 14, dispatch 19); `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` `c512c255` is clean. Right.
- Governed text (Tier S, `.claude/**`): `rest-channel.md` 82/82 — one line added (when a seat may start a run; a workflow joins the allowlist only by its own PR), the quota restatement at the old line 10 deleted (its home is `platform-readings.md`'s quota section), #22457's in-place rewrites intact at lines 48–49 and 74. No re-wrap, no ceiling change, no issue number in operative text.
- Public surface: none. No package publishes any of the six files; `Clause-②: no` is correct.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` on the claim and the PR body; `skip-changeset` is the correct declaration — `scripts/pm/**`, `.github/workflows/**` and `.claude/**` publish nothing. No `.changeset/*.md` touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `actions/create-github-app-token@v3` is a moving major tag: the empty-input skip (`lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js`) was measured by the dev at the tag's current commit (3.2.0). A later v3 that stopped skipping an empty input would fail the mint on every plain stroke — loud, never a silent widening — and the dev's brief asks the maintainer to re-read that line when dependabot bumps the action. Accepted as stated.
- NOT MEASURED until merge, by construction: the first live `workflow_dispatch` stroke (the relay runs `main`'s code); the seat that needs the run (#22014's shard-timings refresh) sends the first one after landing and the read-back names the run or answers UNCONFIRMED.
- Git identity: the first two code commits carry the fleet name with the container e-mail and the earlier merge commit `094be7b5` the container default — the standing observation on the seat post, not a blocker; the final merge commit `e1d81c2a` carries the fleet identity exactly. Trailer pair model-free on every commit.
- The dev's reading at its first report that "#22052's branch sits at `origin/main` with no PR yet" was stale (PR #22457 was open since 10:14Z); the serial landing held anyway — corrected here, no consequence.
- `open_questions`: none. Out-of-scope findings (Acceptance notes, nothing filed): `execute.mjs` imports `PERMISSIONS` and never reads it (pre-existing, lint-clean); three concurrent `check:pm-dispatch-gates` batteries took 18+ minutes each on the shared box (contention, not a defect).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22369-relay-workflow-dispatch-op`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JmWtcHfGbC4ncw4GFKWuRA`

**VERDICT: PASS**
